newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka opposition blames violence on government.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka opposition blames violence on government.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main opposition party on Monday accused President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government of political violence and threatened to boycott parliamentary review of her crucial peace plan.

The United National Party (UNP), ousted from power in 1994 after 17 years of rule by Kumaratunga's People's Alliance, said the government must give up violence towards its supporters if it wanted UNP participation in the plan.

"It has become a problem for us to cooperate with the government in political decision-making," Anura Bandaranaike, Kumaratunga's estranged brother and a UNP member of parliament, told a news conference.
"The time has come for us to decide if we want to continue to cooperate with the govenment on political matters."

The government needs UNP support for a peace plan it proposed last year to end the country's 13-year old ethnic war in which it says 50,000 people have been killed. The plan needs a two-thirds majority in the 225-seat parliament but the UNP has 85 seats.
Bandaranaike, an ardent critic of the government and its policies, was at the centre of the current crisis between the two parties.
He was in a motorcade which was shot at by unidentified gunmen last Friday, when four UNP supporters were killed in the coastal town of Negombo, 25 miles (40 km) north of the capital.
The same night gunmen shot and killed a provincial council member representing the main opposition near Negombo.
Kumaratunga has ordered a special police investigation into the killing. PA members have denied involvement in the incident.
"There has been direct involvement in these events by a leading member of the government," Bandaranaike said. "And his acts of violence have been given maximum endorsement by the head of state."
Kumaratunga last week told a public rally that her supporters would be forced to resort to violence if provoked.
Opposition leader Ranil Wickremesinghe blasted Kumaratunga for "condoning what happened instead of condemning it".
"There must be an end to political violence specially by a government which came to power promising an end to political violence," Wickremesinghe said.
Kumaratunga has publicly criticised the UNP for brutalising opposition supporters and muzzling the media during its rule.

The UNP, which is currently participating in a parliamentary select committee process which is reviewing the peace proposal, has often threatened to pull out of the process, citing attacks on their supporters by alleged government goon squads.
